notes: The flagged unit [s001 s002] → *An evil speaker* is retained as indivisible: *speaker* carries `אִישׁ`'s agent and `לָשׁוֹן`'s speaking together and *evil* answers to neither morpheme, so no source–target allocation between the two nouns is defensible and rule 30's one-rendering condition holds; splitting would leave one noun `unrepresented` beside the other holding the whole rendering, which rule 30 forbids. Head on the governing construct under rule 23, with the indefinite article joining the nominal expression under rule 15.
The ASV's own Hebrew gloss *A man of tongue* corroborates the construct reading and decides nothing (rule 38).

The final *him* was given to the object suffix of `יְצוּדֶנּוּ` rather than left `added` beside a suffix marked `unrepresented`: a present morpheme takes its English before a supplied-word analysis (rule 11), and the count leaves no word unaccounted either way.
